text: t[AA] Is not life on earth a drudgery, [1]its days like those of a hireling?
Like a slave who longs for the shade,a hireling who waits for wages,
So I have been assigned months of futility,and troubled nights have been counted off for me.
When I lie down I say, "When shall I arise?"then the night drags on;I am filled with restlessness until the dawn.
My flesh is clothed with worms and scabs; [AB]my skin cracks and festers;
My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle;they come to an end without hope.
Remember that my life is like the wind; [AC]my eye will not see happiness again.
The eye that now sees me shall no more behold me;when your eye is on me, I shall be gone.
As a cloud dissolves and vanishes, [AD]so whoever goes down to Sheol shall not come up.
They shall not return home again;their place shall know them no more.
My own utterance I will not restrain;I will speak in the anguish of my spirit;I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
t[2] Am I the Sea, or the dragon,that you place a watch over me? [3]
When I say, "My bed shall comfort me,my couch shall ease my complaint,"
Then you frighten me with dreamsand terrify me with visions,
So that I should prefer strangulationand death rather than my existence. [4]
I waste away: I will not live forever; [AE]let me alone, for my days are but a breath.
t[5] What are human beings, that you make much of them,or pay them any heed?
You observe them every morning [AF]and try them at every moment!
How long before you look away from me,and let me alone till I swallow my spit?
If I sin, what do I do to you,O watcher of mortals?Why have you made me your target?Why should I be a burden for you?
Why do you not pardon my offense,or take away my guilt?For soon I shall lie down in the dust;and should you seek me I shall be gone.
